Inference-time steering of a frozen model either guides the sampler by the reward gradient or searches over several trajectories, and recent samplers combine the two.

title: On-Device Adaptive Battery Power Prediction for Electric Vehicles

s2.tldr: This study introduces a novel approach that enables ondevice learning in resource-constrained EV systems to continuously adapt pretrained battery prediction models to new, unseen data, and leverage existing pretrained models by transforming them into adaptable versions that retain critical hyperparameter knowledge from their initial training.

abstractExcerpt: Adaptive power management in Electric Vehicles (EVs) requires accurate power prediction. Although deep learning models have emerged as highly effective for time-series forecasting in this domain, their performance is prone to degradation when exposed to data with distributions different from the training data. We introduce a novel approach that enables on-device learning in resource-constrained EV systems to continuously adapt pretrained battery prediction models to new, unseen data.

title: Metal- and polymer-assisted SEM imaging of protein-bound DNA molecules: a protocol

s2.tldr: This workflow provides a practical framework for preparing stretched DNA samples on silicon wafers and analyzing DNA backbones and associated protein signals by SEM and covers DNA backbone tracing, intensity-profile analysis, and machine-learning-based determination of protein positions from SEM images.

abstractExcerpt: Direct mapping of protein positions along long, stretched DNA molecules requires simultaneous visualization of the DNA backbone and associated protein signals. We recently established a heavy-metal- and polymer-assisted scanning electron microscopy (SEM) approach for imaging stretched DNA molecules and associated protein signals on silicon wafers. Here, we present a practical protocol for implementing this workflow using λ DNA and streptavidin-fluorescent protein-labeled λ DNA as model DNA samples.

abstractExcerpt: As a traditional Chinese medicinal material, the quality of Poria cocos (PC) significantly affects its pharmacological efficacy. However, adulteration of PC in the market has been frequently observed. Adulterated PC not only compromises its medicinal value but also poses potential risks to public health. Conventional identification methods are often labor-intensive, destructive, and insufficiently sensitive to complex adulteration scenarios.

title: ModernMolBERT: A Compact SELFIES Encoder for Molecular Representation Learning
abstractExcerpt: We introduce ModernMolBERT, an encoder-only transformer model for small-molecule representation learning. ModernMolBERT adapts the ModernBERT architecture to molecular language modelling and pairs it with a SELFIES-aware Atom Pair Encoding (APE) tokeniser. Both released variants (small and base) are pre-trained with masked language modelling on approximately 2.4M unique SELFIES strings from ChEMBL 36 and evaluated as frozen molecular embedders on 25 binary classification benchmarks.

title: Resource-efficient energy-based operator selection in fermionic ADAPT-VQE via exact Hamiltonian transformation

s2.tldr: This study shows how exact Hamiltonian transformations provide an effective route to reducing the measurement overhead of fermionic energy-based ADAPT-VQE.

abstractExcerpt: The energy-based approach to operator selection in ADAPT-VQE relies on reconstructing the one-parameter energy landscape for each operator in the pool. In fermionic implementations, the cost of reconstructing this energy landscape often becomes a bottleneck. We address this issue through an exact Hamiltonian transformation that reformulates the one-parameter energy landscape according to a generator-dependent fragmentation of the transformed Hamiltonian.

title: Beyond Numerical Hallucination: Context-Alignment Failures in LLM-Assisted Quantum Dot Synthesis Literature Curation
abstractExcerpt: Reliability work for LLM-assisted materials literature curation has focused on numerical hallucination — fabrication of values absent from source documents. Here we define a recurrent residual failure class, context-alignment failure: cases in which extracted values are source-supported but bound to the wrong sample identity, synthesis stage, measurement state, or source modality. We developed a provenance-preserving four-layer curation workflow with semantic guardrails and human truth-gate review, applied to InP and I–III–VI quantum dot synthesis literature.

abstractExcerpt: Piezoionic sensors perceive the physical world based on polymer ionogels with advantages of flexibility, lightweight, and high sensitivity, and are suitable for physical signal extraction and virtual space construction in artificial intelligence. However, the electrode-electrolyte interface of conventional sensors presents mechanical modulus mismatch, which is prone to interface cracking under external strain and affects cyclic stability.

title: Learning Chemoselectivity in a Low-Data Regime: Bayesian Optimization of the NBS-Activated Selenocyclization of α-Allenols
abstractExcerpt: The activation of diaryl diselenides with N-bromosuccinimide generates two competing electrophiles, and with α-allenols as the π-nucleophiles, product mixtures of brominated and selenylated dihydrofurans can arise. This selectivity challenge was quickly resolved through a Bayesian optimization campaign over seven reaction parameters covering >2000 discrete combinations.

title: Breaking the Potency Barrier: A Practical Recipe for QSAR Extrapolation
abstractExcerpt: Predicting compounds that are more potent than those represented in the training data remains a difficult and practically important problem for quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) modeling. This challenge is particularly relevant during lead optimization, where the goal is to design or identify analogs that are more potent than compounds already measured. To address this problem, we developed a new Pairwise-Difference QSAR (PD-QSAR) approach that learns changes in biological activity from differences in molecular descriptors between compound pairs.

title: Quantum Algorithm for Open-System Battery Cathodes by Modeling Multiple Strongly Coupled Holstein Polarons with Chain-Mapped Caldeira-Leggett Dynamics
abstractExcerpt: Cathode lithiation occupies a chemical regime of tightly localized orbitals, narrow bandwidths, and strong electron-lattice coupling. The defining electrochemical observables (open-circuit voltage and differential capacity) are open-system, reservoir-equilibration quantities that closed-Hamiltonian quantum simulation cannot produce, set by exchange with electron, Li$^+$, and phonon baths. We present a fault-tolerant quantum algorithm that recovers them through a unitary chain-mapped Caldeira-Leggett embedding, rendering the baths Trotterizable.

title: Randomness is All You Need – Studying the Effect of Molecular Conformation on Sigma Profiles as Machine Learning Features
abstractExcerpt: Sigma profiles (SPs) are powerful molecular descriptors that combine the size-independence and continuity of many machine-learned descriptors with the physical interpretability of structural descriptors like molecular graphs or SMILES. Though SPs have existed for a long time within the context of thermodynamic models like COSMO-RS and COSMO-SAC, there does not seem to be a consensus in the literature on the effect of molecular conformations on SPs or on their performance as inputs to thermodynamic or machine learning (ML) models.

We present DolphinQCT, a lightweight, open-source Python tool that samples initial conditions from ORCA frequency calculations and exports them as molecular dynamics restart files. The workflow combines Boltzmann sampling of vibrational energy levels, random-phase normal-mode sampling, and screening based on deviations between electronic and harmonic potential energies.

title: Can AI Help Chemists To Solve NMR?
abstractExcerpt: Chemists read 1 H and 13 C NMR daily, and it is tempting to paste the peak lists into a large language model. Given only those two peak lists for 105 molecules balanced by molecular complexity and compound classes, six frontier LLMs (Claude Opus 4.8, DeepSeek V4 Pro, Gemini 3.1 Pro, GPT-5.5, Grok 4.3, Qwen3.7-Max) and four specialized solvers (BLIND, NMRMind, NMRPeak, NMR-Solver) were compared. The best LLM (Gemini 3.1 Pro) solved 24% of structures, the best specialized model (BLIND) solved 69% of them.

abstractExcerpt: Chemical reaction databases have become core scientific infrastructure. This gap limits the development of machine learning models for organometallic reactions and their applications in mechanism discovery, selectivity prediction, and catalyst design.

abstractExcerpt: The identification and annotation of chemotypes is central to structure–activity relationship studies and property optimization in drug discovery. Current computational approaches rely on predefined fragmentation rules or structural similarity to identify these molecular scaffolds, often overlooking the rich information available in reaction data. Here, we introduce CASyM (Chemotype Annotation through Synthesis Mapping), a novel approach that leverages hierarchical reaction data to systematically identify chemotypes within compound libraries.

abstractExcerpt: Predicting the initiation and propagation of cracks in heterogeneous wellbore systems under complex in-situ conditions remains challenging. We present a hybrid phase-field fracture framework to model crack growth in heterogeneous wellbore systems with weak interfaces. The framework is first validated against benchmark problems with available analytical and numerical solutions. abstractExcerpt: SHP2 supports oncogenic RAS–MAPK signaling, and ligands in its regulatory allosteric pocket can stabilize the autoinhibited state. In a matched benchmark of target-level SHP2 actives and property-matched decoys, the ranking achieved a ROC-AUC of 0.892 and 21.42-fold enrichment in the top 2% of the list.

title: High-throughput identification of ferromagnetic Kagome candidates in the AT6X4 and AT6X5 families
abstractExcerpt: We present a systematic high-throughput density-functional theory study of the thermodynamic stability, collinear magnetic ground states, and electronic structures of layered kagome compounds in the AT6X4 and AT6X5 families. Using the experimentally reported structure types as templates, we screened 78 substitutional compositions in each family. Our calculations reproduce the stability and antiferromagnetic character of the known Fe-based Ge compounds and identify six additional stable candidates with robust ferromagnetism.

title: Specimen design for material parameter identification using topology optimization
abstractExcerpt: Constitutive relations close the equations of continuum mechanics, and serve as a surrogate for a material in the design and engineering process. They are often specified in a parameterized form with parameters identified by experiment. In this paper, we propose a framework for identifying experimental configurations that are maximally informative for material parameter discovery.

title: Separation of Flexible Enantiomers Using Shear Flow
abstractExcerpt: Mechanical separation of enantiomers is an attractive alternative to synthetic methods for producing enantiopure samples. Shear flow that produces solution vorticity has been shown to be a viable means for separating chiral objects on the micro- to nano-scale due to the tensorial nature of the interactions between chiral objects and the surrounding fluid. A recently-developed theory of molecular pitch characterizes these interactions using the resistance tensor and predicts the shear-induced separation of drug-like molecules from their optimized molecular geometries.
